TASK ID: vertex-cover-to-set-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Vertex Cover and TARGET is Set Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

TARGET = SetCover
Set Cover.

Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": k}
  * The universe is the elements 0..u-1.
  * Each set lists distinct elements of the universe, in any order. A set
    may be empty, and the same set may appear more than once.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff AT MOST k of the sets together contain every element of the
universe.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. u = 0 is yes for every k >= 0 (choosing
no sets covers the empty universe). If some element is in no set, the
answer is no.

    reduce(instance) -> instance

+"""Reduction from Vertex Cover to Set Cover.
+
+The source problem (VertexCover) instance format:
+    {"n": int, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": int}
+The target problem (SetCover) instance format:
+    {"universe_size": int, "sets": [[element, ...], ...], "k": int}
+
+We map each edge to a distinct element of the universe (its index in the
+``edges`` list). For each vertex we create a set containing the indices of
+all edges incident to that vertex. Selecting a vertex in the cover is
+equivalent to selecting the corresponding set in the set cover. The
+parameter ``k`` is preserved.
+
+Correctness follows from the standard textbook reduction and respects the
+edge‑case specifications of both problems.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import List, Dict, Any
+
+# Import the problem classes to reuse their validation logic.
+from problems import VertexCover, SetCover
+
+
+def reduce(instance: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Reduce a VertexCover instance to an equivalent SetCover instance.
+
+    The returned instance satisfies ``SetCover.is_yes`` iff the original
+    instance satisfies ``VertexCover.is_yes``.
+    """
+    # Validate the source instance; this will raise InvalidInstance on error.
+    VertexCover.validate(instance)
+
+    n: int = instance["n"]
+    edges: List[List[int]] = instance["edges"]
+    k: int = instance["k"]
+
+    # Universe elements are the edge indices 0 .. m-1 where m = |edges|.
+    m = len(edges)
+    universe_size = m
+
+    # Build a list of sets, one per vertex.
+    # Each set contains the indices of edges incident to that vertex.
+    vertex_sets: List[List[int]] = [[] for _ in range(n)]
+    for idx, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
+        vertex_sets[u].append(idx)
+        vertex_sets[v].append(idx)
+
+    # The target instance format expects a list of sets (list of element lists).
+    target_instance: Dict[str, Any] = {
+        "universe_size": universe_size,
+        "sets": vertex_sets,
+        "k": k,
+    }
+
+    # Validate the constructed target instance to catch programming errors.
+    SetCover.validate(target_instance)
+    return target_instance
+
*** End Patch
PATCH"}
